name: Laying foundations for equitable quality education

content.title: Laying foundations for equitable quality education
content.summary: The Foundations for Learning Project kicks off with a design thinking workshop in Lindi

media.caption: A group photo taken during the design thinking workshop held in Lindi, Tanzania
media.alt: Laying foundations for equitable quality education

content.text: A new project by the Institute for Educational Development, East Africa (IED, EA) in collaboration with the Aga Khan Foundation has officially kicked off. The Foundations for Learning (F4L) project is funded by Global Affairs Canada and the Aga Khan Foundation Canada.

It aims to equip a new generation of learners, teachers and education stakeholders with the knowledge, skills, attitudes and values to lead more gender responsive and pluralist quality education systems. This is in line with the Sustainable Development Goal 4 to ensure inclusive and equitable quality education for all.

Associate Dean at IED, EA Dr Nicholas Wachira noted that involvement of all education stakeholders is crucial for the project to succeed, "The F4L project is built on the goals of transformation of unequal gender norms and power dynamics.Therefore, this project will influence education practices and policies through evidence-based research that will be done throughout the project life."

A two-day design thinking workshop was held in Lindi Municipal, southern Tanzania in December 2021 to plan for implementation of the project. The workshop brought together key government education stakeholders in Tanzania including the Ministry of Education, to familiarize them with the project and get their input on how to best implement it.

Dr Bora Haule, Deputy Regional Education Officer from Lindi Municipal said, "In order to strengthen education systems in our country, we need to build foundations for teachers and learning. It is our responsibility as education stakeholders to support teachers so that they can provide quality education to the students. Through this, the students will then be able to have a sense of self identity and serve their communities well.''
The project is expected to kick off in Lindi, Tanzania in February 2022 and later roll out in Kenya and Uganda.
